correctness.rationale: Direct solution of the backward Robin problem, an exact derivative numerator, strict positivity of its derivative across the entire closed allocation interval, opposite endpoint signs, explicit optimizer formula, implicit crossover/monotonicity proof, and independently checked finite-difference and function-only optimizations. The strong-budget expansions at endpoints are proved using exact roots rather than a nonuniform interior expansion.

evidence: Nicolaou–Mulder, DOI 10.1038/s41598-023-49566-4: numerical exterior-body spatial-reactivity optimization for steady diffusional flux, with a related fixed reactivity resource budget.

The bounded two-endpoint point-start process is eventually absorbed with probability one whenever the total reactivity is positive, so total capture probability cannot distinguish the proposed allocations.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A broader spatial-reactivity budget alone does not imply the present objective: mean time to absorption conditioned on a deterministic start. The flux paper optimizes a different steady-state functional and does not give the exact allocation theorem or strong-budget endpoint square-root law in the examined materials.

originality.rationale: The complete fixed-total-Robin-reactivity unique optimum and its weak/strong allocation laws are not implied by the inspected forward Robin-boundary literature or the separate exterior steady-flux optimization; overlap comparisons include actual searchable records, aliases and stronger-coverage tests. Specialized priority risk remains.
residual_risks: A specialized capture-device, chemical-engineering, or search-theory paper may already derive the exact fixed-sum two-Robin-endpoint theorem under different variable names.
